parsed.title: Discussion on tax filing, domain purchase, and low‑profit app ideas

topics.title: Problems with tax declarations and inspector issues

claims.text: The author paid 500 UAH to aunt Sveta to fix large tax‑declaration errors caused by mis‑labelled columns.
The inspector ignored the author's declarations for 1.5 years and only started demanding re‑verification after being reprimanded in Kyiv.
With Sveta's help the author managed to re‑declare correctly and paid about 1 000 UAH instead of larger fines.
User P2 claimed they haven't bought a domain.
P1 sarcastically suggested someone should buy a calculator first, then there will be money for a domain.
P4 expressed doubt that a domain would be purchased, calling it a “silly thing”.

topics.title: Assessment of a low‑profit web/app project

claims.text: Web platforms are the simplest but far less profitable than Android/iOS apps.
SEO for the web project is poor; even on the 10th Google page the site is not found.
There is no external traffic from social media or contextual ads, and app stores promote new apps more effectively.
User retention is near zero because a paywall appears within the first 10 seconds, deterring buyers.
Conversion rate is assumed to be zero; the product doesn’t simplify tasks nor integrate with banks or tax cabinets.
A successful similar project emphasized very fast delivery (under a week) and a cross‑platform stack (Flutter).
P1 doubts the project's marketability, betting that nobody will buy it within months.
The calculator works only with Ukrainian‑currency (UAH) FOPs; the author had to convert all transactions using the daily exchange rate.

claims.text: P4 jokes that they did not pay 299 UAH for the product and implies the password is stored in local storage as a 100 % discount promo code.
